messages:
mike: heads up — after the canary rollout at 09:14 we saw a spike where clients that reconnect within ~10s got double-billed and console traces show two separate stream sessions attributed to the same request id.

sara: ugh, seen that pattern before. is this the sticky-routing swap we rolled at 09:10? maybe session affinity flipped mid-reconnect.

mike: yeah, sticky routing switch + the new graceful resume window of 15s seems suspect. logs: 
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Resume-Window: 15
X-Request-ID: r_202331234
stream-start session=abc123
stream-reconnect session=abc123 -> session=def456
```

ashley: console product question: are customers seeing duplicate tokens charged or just duplicate lines in the dashboard? need to scope billing impact.

mike: both. small # of requests but definitely double token accounting for reconnecting clients. metrics show token_count++ on both the old and new session for the same client trace id.

jim: oncall checked infra: quota service treats sessions as independent until resume token validated. If the resume window allows >1 open session during route swap, we count both. probable race: resume-accept vs route-open.

observability-team: adding traces — looks like resume handshake completes on the new backend before the old backend gets the close event. telemetry currently attributes tokens to whichever backend processed the chunks; downstream aggregator sums across backends naively.

sara: short-term mitigation idea: when resume header present, attach a resume-tx id in emitted metrics and have aggregator dedupe by resume-tx + request-id within grace window. cheaper than changing billing pipeline quick.

ashley: can we expose that as a console flag? customers might want opt-out for strict billing during their rollouts.

mike: ack. also propose increasing server-side resume check to atomically transfer kv-cache ownership before accepting new session (harder).

jim: rollback option: revert sticky routing swap for the canary cohort while we hotfix aggregator dedupe. oncall can trigger if customers escalate.

observability-team: I pushed a patch to metrics-agg: add a 30s window dedupe by (request-id, resume-tx). Will monitor. (deployed to staging)

deploy-bot: deploy started: metrics-agg/patch-1718901234 -> staging

ashley: thx. I'll add a note in the rollout doc and flag any billing anomalies to finance.

mike: temporary console UX change request: surface "resume-window" in the stream route page and warn if rolling routing policies are enabled concurrently. small change but could prevent this.

sara: agree. I'll make a quick PR to the console; will also add a telemetry alert for >5% duplicate-token rate in 5m window.

jim: leaving this open until we see staging metrics. oncall will keep pager escalation ready.

mike: thanks all — keeping this thread concise. next update in 30m or when staging shows green.
